items.headline: Apache says Roller XML-RPC deserialisation RCE (CVE-2026-129448) is being exploited; same flaw as September's CVE-2026-82384, now extended to 4.0.0–6.1.4
items.summary: On 17 Nov the Apache Software Foundation re-published the Roller pre-authentication XML-RPC deserialisation flaw (CVSS 3.1 9.8) as CVE-2026-129448 for versions 4.0.0–6.1.4 and stated it is being actively exploited; 6.1.6 or later contains the fix. No attacker, victim count or attack detail has been published.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: The Apache Software Foundation's own advisory on the Roller dev list (17 Nov 2026, read via the Mail Archive copy) states 'This issue is being actively exploited' and gives affected and fixed versions. Reported consistently by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Security Affairs, all citing that notice. ASF has published no exploitation evidence, so the extent of exploitation is unverified.
items.firstReported: 11:13 UTC (UK time, GMT) on 17 Nov 2026 (ASF advisory); press coverage from 18 Nov

sections.happened: **Timeline (UK time = UTC in November):** - 25 Sep 2026, 20:12 UTC: Roller PMC member David M. Johnson posts CVE-2026-82384, 'Unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint' (Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8), listing only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected and 6.1.6 or later as the fix (oss-security; Roller dev list). - 27 Sep 2026, 20:59 UTC: Roller 6.1.6 announced as fixing 18 vulnerabilities; the announcement says 6.1.5 is affected and that XML-RPC is vulnerable 'even when disabled' (Roller dev list). - 28 Sep 2026: OSV publishes CVE-2026-82384 (OSV). A third-party PoC page on Pocbit is dated 28 Sep and a GitHub repository with a Python PoC for CVE-2026-82384 exists (Pocbit, GitHub). Corgea says a public PoC has been on GitHub since 28 Sep; the repository's creation date was not confirmed.
sections.technical: **CVE-2026-129448** (CVE-2026-82384 for 6.1.5 only; same flaw per ASF). CWE-502, Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE per OSV record for CVE-2026-82384). **CVSS 3.1 9.8 (ASF):** `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`. **Root cause (ASF):** the XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserialises them before authenticating the requester. The September notice adds that the servlet is mapped unconditionally, so request parsing and deserialisation occur even when the global XML-RPC feature is set to disabled, and that no non-default configuration is required. **Mechanism (from the project's fix and third-party write-ups):** the fix pull request (apache/roller PR 171) describes the servlet as configured to accept the library's non-standard vendor extension types, which Roller does not use.
sections.guidance: **Apache Software Foundation (advisory, 17 Nov):** upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled. For users who cannot upgrade immediately: set `enabledForExtensions` to `false` in `WEB-INF/web.xml`, or remove the `/roller-services/xmlrpc` servlet mapping, and restart Roller.
sections.differing: **Affected-version scope:** the September notice listed only 6.1.5. The November notice says the same flaw affects 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and lists affected versions as '4.0.0 before 6.1.5' while its CVE title says 'releases before 6.1.5'. Some secondary summaries describe the range as 4.0.0 through 6.1.5; ASF assigns 6.1.5 to the earlier CVE, so the combined range is both records. **Exploitation:** only ASF asserts exploitation.
sections.unknown: - Who is exploiting the flaw, how many servers are affected, what attackers did after access, and whether exploitation began before or after the 25 Sep disclosure and the public PoC. - Whether CISA will add CVE-2026-129448 to KEV.

items.headline: Bitdefender: suspected China-linked group rebuilt EggStreme malware and is still targeting Philippine government organisations
items.summary: Bitdefender reports the suspected China-linked EggStreme operators rebuilt their toolkit with a new protocol, more commands and a passive backdoor variant, still targeting Philippine government organisations.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Single vendor research report; attribution suspected; victims unnamed.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Bitdefender report and The Hacker News coverage, both dated 18 Nov; exact UK time not confirmed)

sections.happened: Bitdefender's 18 November 2026 report says the suspected Chinese APT behind EggStreme rebuilt its malware after exposure. Newer builds use a different network protocol, an enhanced command set and a passive variant that does not beacon out. Bitdefender assesses with high confidence that multiple Philippine government organisations were affected. Victims are not named.
sections.technical: Newer EggStremeAgent builds replaced gRPC with direct TCP while keeping mutual TLS; a passive variant waits for inbound connections. Keylogger omitted from observed builds; added domain mapping, system queries and in-memory PowerShell. Sideloaded DLLs under system library names, SMB file-share staging, in-memory execution. Initial access not determined.
sections.guidance: No vendor patch applies; this is a malware campaign. Bitdefender's report publishes indicators of compromise and detection notes.
sections.differing: Bitdefender says overlap with CL-STA-1048 (Palo Alto Networks) is unassessed; it did not compare infrastructure. Possible Taiwan targeting is low-to-medium confidence.
sections.unknown: Initial access vector, victim count and identities, and whether the activity is government-directed remain undetermined in public reporting.

items.firstReported: 18 November 2026 (Wednesday), TechCabal, citing the airline's ShebaMiles email notice; other outlets followed the same day

sections.happened: Ethiopian Airlines emailed ShebaMiles frequent-flyer members on Wednesday 18 November 2026 about a recent cyberattack that may have exposed some information. It gave no intrusion date, data categories or member count. It said there was currently no evidence financial information was accessed. The notice came two weeks after Air Botswana's 4 November notice of a suspected ransomware attack detected on 3 November.
sections.technical: No technical details published: intrusion date, initial access, malware, actor and indicators of compromise are all unknown. Air Botswana's incident was described as suspected ransomware; no public link to the Ethiopian Airlines incident has been reported.
sections.guidance: The airline urged members to remain vigilant against suspicious or unsolicited communications and said it would provide updates as the investigation continues.
sections.differing: Per Daily News Egypt, citing BBC, the BBC's requests for more detail were unsuccessful and no website statement had been published by Wednesday evening.
sections.unknown: Intrusion date, data categories, number of members affected, whether bookings or flight operations were touched, and whether ShebaMiles was the only system involved.

items.headline: GTA VI launch used in scams, fake downloads and malware targeting accounts and crypto wallets
items.summary: Scammers are exploiting GTA VI launch hype with fake free codes, Google sign-in phishing, fake Android and PC downloads, crypto wallet drainers and infostealers. Malwarebytes and NordVPN report the activity.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Security vendors' research reports; no Rockstar or Take-Two statement seen.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 14:07 UK time (TechRadar, reporting NordVPN research); Malwarebytes blog 22:06 UK time

sections.happened: Malwarebytes (published 18 Nov) reports scam sites offering 'free' GTA VI codes, pre-orders and map downloads, fake Google sign-in pages, fake Android downloads, crypto token promotions and wallet-connect traps. NordVPN told TechRadar (18 Nov) that its Threat Intelligence team found a $200 dark-web malware kit on 16 Nov, ahead of the 19 Nov console launch.
sections.technical: NordVPN kit: fake 'GTA6 Keygen.exe' cookie stealer capturing browser session tokens, crypto wallet drainer for Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana and Polygon, and XMRig cryptominer. Malwarebytes: phishing page mimics Google sign-in. No CVEs identified.
sections.guidance: Malwarebytes: buy only from official stores; uninstall any GTA 6 APK; revoke unknown wallet approvals; change Google passwords via Google's site and enable 2-Step Verification. NordVPN: never run key generators or cracks.
sections.unknown: Scale and victim numbers not reported. Computer Weekly and Help Net Security articles were not read. Rockstar has not announced an Android or iOS version, and no PC version date is confirmed.

items.headline: Wellington IT breach exposes payee data at about 40 Irish credit unions; delayed notification criticised
items.summary: Belfast-based software provider Wellington IT notified about 40 Irish credit unions of an October 2026 intrusion exposing saved payee details. Minister of State Robert Troy called the delay in notifying them 'not acceptable'. Total affected is unknown.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Wellington IT CEO statement and several affected credit unions confirm incident; scale unverified.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (date per Irish Times URL; exact UK time not confirmed), Irish Times

sections.happened: Wellington IT, a Belfast-based provider of the CU Online banking platform used by many Irish credit unions, notified customers of a cyber incident. Per Irish Examiner-seen notices, attacker activity ran 2-4 October 2026. Payee records were accessed; passwords, PINs, card details and balances reportedly unaffected. Minister Robert Troy called the notification delay 'not acceptable'.
sections.technical: Per customer notices as reported: an automated script made about five million requests to exploit an authorization flaw, accessing private records with valid credentials. Wellington IT said it lacked activity logs to determine which member payee data was compromised. No CVE or ATT&CK mapping published.
sections.guidance: Members advised to remain vigilant for unexpected calls, texts or emails about credit union accounts or payments (RTÉ, citing credit unions). Data Protection Commission investigating.
sections.differing: Scale differs: about 40 (RTÉ, BleepingComputer), 43 (Irish Times headline), 50 credit unions across sources. Irish Times says up to 1.8 million people could be affected; RTÉ says hundreds of thousands. Total impact unknown.
sections.unknown: Exact number of affected members and payees; method of initial access; attacker identity; whether data is for sale.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities reports breach of test environment exposing up to 15.72 million accounts
items.summary: Japanese broker Rakuten Securities disclosed unauthorised access to a test environment holding unmasked production customer data, potentially exposing up to 15.72 million accounts. Passwords and PINs reportedly not taken.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company publicly disclosed and apologised; figures are from its statement as reported.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (JST) via company apology, per Infosecurity Magazine; UK time not stated

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities said on 17 Nov 2026 it discovered unauthorised access on 16 Nov. Customer information in a test environment may have leaked on 11 Nov. About 4.47 million accounts had personal and financial details exposed; 11.25 million had branch codes and login IDs exposed. No evidence of account misuse was reported.
sections.technical: Test environment held unmasked production customer data, copied there during a system upgrade. Mallory reports attackers exploited a vulnerability the company did not publicly identify. No CVE, ATT&CK mapping or IOCs published.
sections.guidance: Rakuten Securities warned customers about targeted phishing and urged adoption of FIDO2 passkeys, which it said over 90% of customers already use.
sections.differing: Infosecurity Magazine says nearly 16 million; Japan Times and Mallory say up to 15.72 million. The figures reconcile as 4.47 million plus 11.25 million.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, the exploited vulnerability, the transfer timing and the full scope remain undisclosed. Investigation is ongoing with outside parties.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline; about 265,000 customer accounts may have been compromised
items.summary: TfL says around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had account details (contact details, dates of birth, security questions and answers) compromised after suspicious activity on 16 November; the photocard website remains offline and TfL has notified the ICO.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Rests on TfL's own statement (Shashi Verma, director of technology strategy and revenue), quoted consistently by The Register, ianVisits, the BBC, the Telegraph and Sky News (via syndicated text), and on the text of TfL's email to affected customers as reported by Sky News. TfL says it has notified the ICO. TfL's own web pages and Infosecurity Magazine could not be fetched, so the statement was read as quoted by outlets. No attacker claim, ICO statement or technical write-up was found.

sections.happened: Mon 16 Nov 2026: TfL says it became aware that Oyster photocard customers were receiving emails asking them to create an account when they already had one. TfL told The Register the emails came from its own systems but were generated as a result of the compromise. It took the photocard website down immediately (The Register; ianVisits; Sky News text). Wed 18 Nov: TfL said around 265,000 photocard customers may have had account details compromised and that the incident had been contained. TfL began contacting affected customers that day, and a Sky News report quotes TfL's email saying 'suspicious activity' on 16 November 'resulted in unauthorised access to the personal information contained in your web account' (ianVisits; Sky News via Great Driffield Radio). First published coverage located: Britbrief at 20:45 UK, carrying TfL's statement; Telegraph text via Yahoo at 22:26 UK.
sections.technical: Attack vector, entry point and attacker identity have not been disclosed by TfL (The Register; IBTimes UK). The only technical indicator published is the unsolicited 'create an account' emails sent from TfL's own systems to existing account holders (The Register). Infosecurity Magazine describes these as sent by 'unauthorized actors' from TfL's system; this is the outlet's characterisation. No CVE, malware, tooling, IOCs or MITRE ATT&CK mapping have been published. Data TfL says may be affected: names, email addresses, home addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, security questions and answers. TfL's current assessment is that passwords, bank or payment card details, journey information, and names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised.
sections.guidance: TfL, as published: all photocard customers will be asked to change their password and security question and answer; TfL advises changing the password on any other online service where the same information is used (Register; BBC text; Britbrief copy of TfL statement). TfL says there is currently no evidence the data has been used (The Register).
sections.differing: TfL says 'around 265,000' customers 'may have had' account details compromised and that, because of the speed of its response, the number who could have been affected 'was significantly reduced' (Verma, quoted by ianVisits and Sky News text). Some outlets phrase the position more firmly: the BBC text says details 'have been accessed' and 'were compromised'; the Telegraph headline says hackers 'steal' names and dates of birth.
sections.unknown: How attackers gained access and whether it was an application flaw, credential abuse or other method. Who is responsible; no claim has been reported. Whether any data has been misused or published. Whether the 265,000 figure will change (TfL says 'may have' and that investigation continues).

items.headline: N-able confirms unauthorised access to a Mail Assure/SpamExperts Hosted Cloud server; management portal and APIs offline in three regions since 16–18 Nov
items.summary: N-able says an intruder accessed one server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud; management UI, APIs, quarantine and logging remain offline in Americas, APAC and Europe while mail filtering continues. No evidence of customer data or mailbox access so far; attacker, entry method and dwell time not disclosed.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: N-able's own status-page incident (uptime.n-able.com/event/202672), as quoted by The Hacker News and relayed by Cyber Security News, Cyber Press and The CyberSec Guru, states unauthorised access to one server. The status page itself could not be fetched, so wording is taken from those quotations; vendor details are thin (no actor, vector, duration or scope of access).
items.firstReported: 16 Nov (customer notice of disruption); breach disclosed 18 Nov 03:05 UK; THN article 19 Nov

sections.happened: **Mon 16 Nov 2026:** N-able first told customers about a service disruption in the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment (per Cyber Security News, The Hacker News). **Tue 17 Nov:** a formal status incident opened at 03:00 UTC (= UK time); by 06:10 the symptom was described as dashboard access affected with mail filtering still operating. At 13:33 UTC N-able attributed the issue to "a combination of platform configuration and service dependencies" and said remediation required rebuilding affected infrastructure and updating platform components (The CyberSec Guru, quoting the status page). **Wed 18 Nov, 03:05 UK:** N-able updated to say it was aware of unauthorised access to one of the servers, that it had proactively disabled UI and API access, and that email flow and spam filtering continued unaffected (The CyberSec Guru, quoting the status page).
sections.technical: Vector, technique, actor, malware and IOCs: none published by N-able. No CVE or CVSS associated. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping can be made from public information. N-able's stated position (quoted by The Hacker News): "We have taken steps to mitigate the threat and are continuing to harden our services to reduce the risk of recurrence. The investigation is ongoing, but at this time we do not have evidence that customer data was compromised, including access to tenants' mailboxes." Cyber Security News, Cyber Press and The CyberSec Guru each note this describes an ongoing investigation, not a final finding. The initial "configuration/dependencies" root-cause statement of 17 Nov was withdrawn about 14 hours later (The CyberSec Guru's calculation from the status-page timestamps).
sections.guidance: Published by N-able (via the outlets quoted): partners have been contacted directly with information relevant to their environment and whether action is required; the management portal, APIs, quarantine and logging will be restored once security validation is complete.
sections.differing: No conflicting accounts about the breach itself. Headline framing varies: The Hacker News says "hackers breach"; N-able says "unauthorized access" and has identified no actor. Cyber Press's headline refers to "credential exposure", but its body says the public updates did not confirm credential exposure or identify any affected passwords, API keys or tokens.
sections.unknown: Who accessed the server, how, when access began, how long it lasted, and what privileges were gained. The server's role. Whether any credentials, API keys, tokens, quarantined message content or logs were accessible from it (N-able says no evidence of customer-data compromise so far).

items.headline: F5 fixes six critical BIG-IP flaws enabling unauthenticated TMM crashes, possible RCE
items.summary: F5 disclosed six critical BIG-IP data-plane flaws (CVSS v3.1 9.8) that let unauthenticated attackers crash the Traffic Management Microkernel in specific virtual-server configurations. Fixes are engineering hotfixes only; no workaround.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: F5 advisories reported via The Hacker News; primary F5 page unreadable.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (date per The Hacker News; exact UK time not stated); first source The Hacker News

sections.happened: F5 disclosed six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities on 18 November 2026, rated 9.8 (CVSS v3.1) and 9.3 (CVSS v4.0). Unauthenticated attackers can crash the Traffic Management Microkernel, disrupting traffic until restart; F5 says they may also allow remote code execution. WatchTowr's Sina Kheirkhah reported four. None reported exploited.
sections.technical: Stack-based buffer overflows in the BIG-IP data plane. Triggers need specific virtual-server settings: iRules using PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address, GENERICMESSAGE::route or DNS::scrape, or an APM per-request policy with Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. CVEs: 2026-123637, -121805, -120292, -120285, -116953, -120722.
sections.guidance: Per F5 advisories as reported: install the engineering hotfix (no workaround listed). Hotfixes lack full QA and carry no warranty. Custom hotfixes need a new build from F5 support.
sections.differing: CVE-2026-120722: F5's advisory lists BIG-IP CNF as not vulnerable; its updated CVE record lists CNF as affected.
sections.unknown: Primary F5 advisory K000164058 was unreadable; fixed BIG-IP builds for most CVEs not confirmed. Exploitation status after publication unknown.

items.headline: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): OpenJDK Base64 flaw fixed 17 Nov; probing and exploit attempts reported, no confirmed compromise, several vendor fixes still pending
items.summary: A heap overflow in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder (17.0.6+, 21, 25, 27) was patched by Oracle and OpenJDK on 17 Nov. Calif reports pre-auth RCE in six enterprise products; GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian report probing and exploit attempts but no confirmed intrusion, while Atlassian, Cisco, Siemens and Elastic fixes are still due.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Rests on Oracle's November CSPU credit for CVE-2026-114938, the OpenJDK advisory and fixed builds (as relayed by Canada's Cyber Centre, CERT-EU, Cisco, Keycloak, Jenkins), vendor advisories from Red Hat, Cisco, Atlassian, Elastic and Siemens, and the CISA alert. The flaw is confirmed. Remote code execution rests on Calif's demonstrations plus unpublished exploits claimed by VulnCheck and Immersive; independent labs have published crash and memory-leak reproductions only. Exploitation attempts are sensor reports from several firms; no successful compromise is confirmed.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov (Calif post on X, time not shown); latest development SecurityWeek 19 Nov 09:10 UK

sections.happened: **17 Nov (UK = UTC):** Calif said on X it had found and reported the flaw and that details had leaked (cited by The Hacker News and The Register). At 21:00 Oracle's November Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory were released (per Cloudflare); Calif published its write-up the same day. CISA issued an alert dated 17 Nov, with Canada's Cyber Centre contributing. **18 Nov:** Cisco (16:00), Keycloak, Jenkins, Siemens, Elastic and Atlassian published advisories; Switzerland's NCSC issued a warning. **19 Nov (latest):** SecurityWeek (09:10) reports GreyNoise logged 150+ attack-shaped requests from five IPs, watchTowr honeypots saw `java4shell-recon` User-Agent spraying and blind exploit attempts, Cloudflare saw scanners concealing tooling, and Previdian logged nine attempts from six IPs. None is confirmed successful. Keycloak (updated 08:00 UTC) now ships images 26.8.2-3 on Red Hat OpenJDK 21.0.13.1.
sections.technical: **Flaw:** heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-122, per Canada's Cyber Centre) in HotSpot's x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI Base64 decode intrinsic. A padding bug underflows the output length, so a full 64-byte masked store overruns the buffer by 62 bytes (trigger: 64 `A` plus `=`; 128 on JDK 17). Java rejects the input only afterwards. **Preconditions:** OpenJDK 17.0.6+, 21, 25, 27, Oracle Java SE 8 performance build and GraalVM; CPU with avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi, bmi2 (Intel Ice Lake+, AMD Zen 4+); attacker-controlled Base64 reaching `java.util.Base64.Decoder`. ARM64 and standard Java 8/11 are not affected. **Exploitation (Calif):** remote heap grooming gives a bounded write and read-back ("JavaBleed"), then code execution; no universal exploit, failed attempts can crash the JVM. Pre-auth RCE shown: Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, PingFederate; post-auth: Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, Spinnaker. Calif's PoC only triggers corruption.
sections.guidance: **Oracle/OpenJDK:** fixed Java SE 8u513, 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1; GraalVM 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1; GraalVM EE 21.3.20.1. Amazon, Azul, Microsoft have builds out; Temurin rolling out. **Red Hat, Keycloak, Jenkins, CERT-EU:** interim `-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics` (Calif also `-XX:UseAVX=2`, x86-64 only). **Atlassian:** Data Center patches pending; interim `-XX:UseAVX=2`. **Cisco:** no workarounds, fixes TBD. **Siemens:** Industrial Edge Management unfixed; offline advised. **Elastic:** fix due in 8.19.26, 9.4.10, 9.5.7, 9.6.0.
sections.differing: **Severity:** Calif 9.2 (CVSS 4.0); Oracle 8.1 (CVSS 3.1, high complexity); Red Hat preliminary 9.8 and Amazon 8.8 (per The Hacker News); Atlassian 9.2 for Data Center. **RCE ease:** VulnCheck says DoS is trivial and RCE needs heavy grooming; Blackpoint reproduced crash and leak, not RCE; Wiz says it built a PoC in two hours. Only Calif's demos show RCE publicly.
sections.unknown: Whether any attempt succeeded; who is behind the probing; CISA KEV status (not listed on 17–18 Nov, not rechecked); number of exposed systems; Red Hat, Temurin, Atlassian, Cisco, Siemens and Elastic fix dates; when Calif releases product exploits.

items.headline: NGINX 'nginx2root': five unauthenticated-RCE flaws fixed in 1.31.9/1.30.7; public PoC for HTTP/2 bug CVE-2026-123007; no exploitation reported as of 19 Nov
items.summary: F5/nginx fixed ten NGINX flaws on 18 Nov, five of them (CVSS 4.0 9.2) able to give worker-level code execution; the HTTP/2 flaw CVE-2026-123007 dates to nginx 1.9.5 (2015). Rapid7 and Censys proof-of-concept code is public; F5 and CERT-EU report no exploitation. Latest: Ubuntu and AlmaLinux fixed packages out, Debian fix in unstable only, more national CERT warnings, Censys tracker shows about 8.8 million exposed services (per a secondary report).
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 and the nginx project published advisories, release notes and fixed versions on 18 Nov 2026 (nginx.org advisories page and CHANGES read directly; F5 K-articles did not render). Five research teams (Xint, Wiz, Rapid7, Metnir, Ikotas Labs) published or announced findings; Rapid7's exploit was reproduced by Censys; CERT-EU and CIRCL published advisories, and CERT-FR, NCSC-NL, CERT-Bund, JPCERT/CC and others issued alerts (as listed by Precursor Security).

sections.happened:
**Latest developments (to about 12:40 UK, 19 Nov 2026; UK = GMT).**
- **Exploitation status unchanged.** The Hacker News (18 Nov), SecurityWeek (19 Nov, 10:26 UK), CERT-EU (advisory 2026-022, 18 Nov), Qualys (18 Nov) and Censys (18 Nov) report no known exploitation in the wild. F5 told The Register (21:11 UTC, 18 Nov) it had found no evidence of active exploitation. The Hacker News reported CISA's KEV catalogue did not list the flaw as of 18 Nov; the KEV page itself was not readable for this item. - **Distribution fixes.** Canonical's USN-9159-1 (dated 19 Nov) lists fixed nginx packages for Ubuntu 26.10, 26.04, 24.04 and 22.04 and ESM releases back to 16.04 (Precursor Security timestamps it 05:21 GMT).
sections.technical:
**CVEs (F5 rates each CVSS 4.0 9.2; CERT-EU and Qualys also quote CVSS 3.1 8.1):**
- **CVE-2026-123007** - HTTP/2 flow-control integer underflow/overflow (CWE-191 per Rapid7) causing an out-of-bounds heap copy. Needs HTTP/2 enabled. nginx.org: vulnerable 1.9.5-1.31.8. Wiz showed code execution on nginx serving static files over TLS on 64-bit official 1.31.7/1.31.8 builds. - **CVE-2026-123633** - HTTP/2 use-after-free when connection draining closes a connection during upstream connection setup (needs proxying and low worker_connections). nginx.org: 1.19.7-1.31.8. - **CVE-2026-121810** - same pattern over HTTP/3/QUIC with upstream proxying. nginx.org: 1.25.0-1.31.8. - **CVE-2026-123634** - resolver use-after-free (needs `resolver` and a request-derived proxy target; Xint tested via `mirror`; F5 per The Hacker News also names SSI). nginx.org: 0.6.18-1.31.8. - **CVE-2026-113425** - mail-proxy use-after-free during `auth_http` lookup. nginx.org: 0.5.33-1.31.8. Code runs as the nginx worker, not root.
sections.guidance: **F5 / nginx project:** nginx Open Source 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable) fix all ten flaws (nginx.org CHANGES). NGINX Plus fixed in 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1; the CVE-2026-123633 fix was in earlier builds 37.2.0.1 and 37.0.7.1; The Hacker News and Rapid7 report no fix listed for NGINX Plus R34-R36. F5 states code execution requires ASLR to be disabled or bypassed (per SecurityWeek, Qualys).
sections.differing: **Severity scoring.** F5 rates all five CVSS 4.0 9.2 (Critical); CERT-EU and Qualys quote CVSS 3.1 8.1. nginx.org's own page rates CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-113425 'major' and CVE-2026-123633, -121810 and -123634 'medium'. These are different scales, not a factual conflict. **ASLR.** F5 (per SecurityWeek, Qualys) says code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed.
sections.unknown: - Whether any exploitation is occurring or will follow the public PoCs; CISA KEV and UK NCSC pages were not read. - F5 advisories K000163925-K000163931 and K000164058 did not render, so F5's own wording is taken from nginx.org, secondary reports and researchers.

items.headline: PHP schedules critical security release for all supported versions on 19 November; CVE-2026-115560 RCE expected to be fixed
items.summary: PHP's security team pre-announced releases for 14:00–14:30 UTC on 19 Nov with top severity CRITICAL (non-default or uncommon setups only); CVE-2026-115560, a session-upload-progress RCE disclosed on 23 Oct, is expected to be covered. No release had been published at about 12:35 UK.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Rests on the PHP project's own php.net notices (18 Nov pre-announcement; 23 Oct informational advisory naming CVE-2026-115560). Fixed versions, the full CVE list and CVSS scores are not yet published, so details are thin; reports that CVE-2026-115560 will be fixed in this release come from The Register, SecurityWeek and The Hacker News inferring from the 23 Oct notice (PHP said a full advisory would come with the next regular release).
items.firstReported: 18 Nov (php.net notice, time not shown on the page); The Register 22:38 UK, SecurityWeek 07:45 UK on 19 Nov

sections.happened: **Timeline (UK time; UK is on GMT, equal to UTC, in November):** - 21 Oct 2026: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 out of cycle for two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (collectively PHP2Shell) (php.net). - 23 Oct 2026: PHP published an informational advisory for a third issue, CVE-2026-115560, saying it would be handled in the regular release cycle and a full advisory would be published with the next release (php.net). - 18 Nov 2026 (time not shown on php.net): the PHP security team announced security releases scheduled for Thursday 19 Nov between 14:00 and 14:30 UK time, part of the regular four-week cycle, addressing vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions. The highest severity is CRITICAL, and the issues rated critical require 'either non-default configuration or uncommon setups' (php.net).
sections.technical: **CVE-2026-115560** (named by The Register, SecurityWeek and The Hacker News; the 23 Oct php.net advisory gives the conditions but does not state the CVE in the 18 Nov notice): remote code execution via the session upload progress feature. PHP states that exposure requires all of the following: an application sets `session.serialize_handler` to `php_binary` or `php_serialize` in its configuration, then switches it to `php` at runtime with `ini_set()` before calling `session_start()`; and session upload progress is still enabled (php.net). The Hacker News and Aikido say upload progress is on by default. PHP has not published affected versions, a CVSS score, a CWE or an ATT&CK mapping for this CVE. Aikido states the 21 Oct releases do not fix it.
sections.guidance: **PHP project (php.net):** - 18 Nov: users are 'strongly encouraged to prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available'; technical details and fixed version numbers will be published alongside the releases. - 23 Oct: set `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` until the next regular bugfix release to protect from the CVE-2026-115560 RCE vector. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled.
sections.differing: **Severity wording.** PHP rates the highest issue CRITICAL but states that critical issues require non-default configuration or uncommon setups. The PHP Foundation's Barron said CVE-2026-115560 is not expected to occur in practical use.
sections.unknown: - Fixed version numbers, the complete CVE list, CVSS scores and the full advisory text; PHP says they arrive with the release. - Which issues other than CVE-2026-115560 are rated Critical, and the 'uncommon setup' each needs.

items.headline: Nvidia stops licensed H200 shipments to China; US extends remote-access licensing to overseas Chinese-headquartered tenants
items.summary: Nvidia said on its Q3 FY2027 earnings call it has stopped shipping export-licensed Hopper data center chips to China. Commerce issued a remote-access interim final rule on 16 November.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Halt quoted via secondary reports of the call; release confirms quarter figures only.
items.firstReported: Nov 18, 2026 (UK time not verified); earnings call 17 Nov 2026 US time, reported same night by The Verge per secondary source

sections.happened: On its 17 November earnings call, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said the company is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China. Those products generated $2.4 billion in the quarter ended 25 October. Separately, a Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security interim final rule of 16 November requires licences for advanced AI chips in data centres supplying large compute to China-headquartered firms.
sections.differing: Jefferies estimates the remote-access rule could cut Nvidia's 2027 data center revenue by $44bn to $62bn; Kress said backlog for Vera Rubin means no top-line hit. Jefferies figure is an analyst estimate.
sections.unknown: Reasons for the halt not officially stated. Tencent and other Chinese firms' reactions and the source articles' details were not verified. Status of about 600,000 H200s reportedly held in Hong Kong is unclear.

items.headline: Anthropic prices record $81.3bn IPO at $83 per share, above target range
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its $70-$78 range, selling about 980 million shares for $81.3bn, the largest IPO on record. Nasdaq trading as ANT is expected Thursday.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Multiple major outlets (CNBC, CNN, Reuters-sourced reports) cite the company's press release and filings
items.firstReported: Wednesday 18 November 2026 evening UK time (pricing); first source not confirmed from read pages

sections.happened: Anthropic priced its IPO on Wednesday 18 November at $83 per share, above the $70-$78 range, after upsizing from 825 million to about 980 million shares. The offering raised about $81.3bn at a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5tn. Trading is expected on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday.
sections.differing: Reports differ on figures: some early reports used the original 825 million-share deal. Axios cites $79.4bn raised before fees from company shares. Later reports use the upsized figures.
sections.unknown: First-day trading price, whether underwriters exercise their option to buy up to 147 million additional shares, and post-listing performance. Ynetnews, citing Reuters, reports the offering is expected to close on 20 November.
